findings.issue: The new guard can never fail. In a Java string literal, "\b" is the backspace escape (U+0008), not the regex word boundary. So the pattern "(?i)\b(ALTER|DROP|TRUNCATE)\b" in the source looks for a backspace character, then the keyword, then another backspace. It never matches real SQL, and the test passes even if V6 contains DROP TABLE. This change made the check weaker than before: the old doesNotContain("DROP ") at least caught 'DROP '. Now nothing guards the 'additive' half of AC-9 in tests. V6 itself is unchanged and is still only CREATE TABLE and CREATE INDEX statements, so production is fine; only the guard is broken.
findings.fix: Escape the backslash: doesNotContainPattern("\\b(ALTER|DROP|TRUNCATE)\\b"). The (?i) is redundant after toUpperCase(), so drop one of the two. Optionally add a sanity assertion that the same pattern matches a sample string such as "DROP\nTABLE x", so the test cannot silently go vacuous again.

findings.issue: emptyPayloadsAreCorrupt seeds attempts=19, so the row goes DEAD on any failure. verify(kafka, never()) proves the corrupt check runs before send, but the test never checks why the row died.

findings.issue: cancelledDuringBlockerCheckIsNotErased asserts runDue(...) isZero(). That assumes no other due SCHEDULED request exists in the shared DB. forcedFailureRollsBack cleans up its leftover, but any other test class that leaves a due request would make this test flaky. The sibling tests use isGreaterThanOrEqualTo for this reason.
findings.fix: Optionally drop the return-value assertion. The status, profile, address and outbox assertions on u already prove the guard.

summary: Four of the five prior findings are resolved, and so are both security fixes. The fifth, the migration regex, brings in a new defect, so the verdict is request_changes. (1) Guarded UPDATE: the new IT makes the privacyHttp blocker stub cancel the request in the middle of runDue. It then asserts the status is CANCELLED, the email is unchanged, the address remains and there are 0 outbox rows. Removing the SCHEDULED guard or the claimed==0 return would now fail it. (2) Corrupt payload: deliver() throws the constant 'Corrupt outbox payload' IllegalStateException for a null event or a null userId, before any send. The IT covers jsonb 'null' and '{}'. (3) Admin status: the value is upper-cased with Locale.ROOT, and anything other than DEAD or PENDING raises CodedException VALIDATION_FAILED. The MVC test asserts 400 for DONE and 200 for lowercase pending. A blank value also gets 400, which is acceptable. (4) describe() now uses the root cause's class and message, truncated to 500. The AC-10 corrupt path still has no cause, so no Jackson or PII text can reach last_error. The test covers the wrapped case and the truncation. (5) Migration regex: not resolved. The Java literal "\b" is a backspace, so the new assertion is vacuous and weaker than the check it replaced (major). Security: enqueue checks the update count and logs one WARN that carries only the userId when ON CONFLICT suppresses a duplicate. The OutputCapture test checks that the line appears only on the second call and does not contain the email domain. Apart from that, the delta adds no defect: the try/catch in deliver still turns only JsonProcessingException into the constant message, and the relay loop marks the row failed or DEAD as before. AC-9 is still met in substance, because V6 is unchanged and I read it as additive, but its non-destructive guard in tests must be fixed. AC-11 now rests on the recorded verify.md.
